lesson_scope: Combined complex loci with argument and modulus boundaries, shaded planar regions, disk-half-plane intersections, annuli, circular sectors, circular segments and overlapping lenses, perimeter and area calculations.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Annulus region description and exact area calculation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Annulus area between concentric circles.

hints: Recognise concentric circles centred at $1 + 3\mathrm{i}$ with inner radius $2$ and outer radius $5$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify geometry of annulus:
$$\text{Concentric circles centred at } 1 + 3\mathrm{i} \text{ with radii } r_1 = 2 \text{ and } r_2 = 5$$

Calculate exact area:
$$\text{Area} = \pi r_2^2 - \pi r_1^2 = \pi(25 - 4) = 21\pi$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies annulus centred at $1 + 3\mathrm{i}$ with radii $2$ and $5$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Sector area and perimeter from argument boundaries.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Sector area and perimeter from modulus and argument bounds.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate sector area:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} R^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(36)\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 6\pi$$

Calculate sector perimeter:
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2R + R\theta = 2(6) + 6\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 12 + 2\pi$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Simplifying modulus inequality to linear half-plane.

walkthrough.text:
Expand squared distances:
$$x^2 + y^2 \leqslant (x - 4)^2 + y^2$$
$$x^2 \leqslant x^2 - 8x + 16$$

Solve inequality:
$$8x \leqslant 16 \implies x \leqslant 2$$
$$\text{Region: points on and to the left of the line } x = 2$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Expressing a sector region as complex inequalities.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Writing modulus and argument inequalities from geometric description.

walkthrough.text:
Write the modulus boundary:
$$|z| \leqslant 3$$

Write the argument boundary:
$$\frac{\pi}{6} \leqslant \arg(z) \leqslant \frac{3\pi}{4}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Point-testing against combined modulus and argument inequalities.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Testing candidate points against combined loci.

walkthrough.text:
Test $z_1 = 1 + \mathrm{i}$:
$$|z_1 - 2\mathrm{i}| = |1 - \mathrm{i}| = \sqrt{2} \leqslant 2, \quad \arg(z_1) = \frac{\pi}{4} \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{4}\right] \implies \text{Inside}$$

Test $z_2 = 2 + 2\mathrm{i}$ and $z_3 = \mathrm{i}$:
$$|z_2 - 2\mathrm{i}| = |2| = 2 \leqslant 2, \quad \arg(z_2) = \frac{\pi}{4} \implies \text{On boundary (inside)}$$
$$|z_3 - 2\mathrm{i}| = |-\mathrm{i}| = 1 \leqslant 2, \quad \arg(z_3) = \frac{\pi}{2} > \frac{\pi}{4} \implies \text{Outside}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Circular segment area from disk and vertical line.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Calculating segment area between circle and vertical line.

walkthrough.text:
Find central angle:
$$\cos\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{\pi}{3} \implies \theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}$$

Calculate segment area:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} R^2 (\theta - \sin\theta) = \frac{1}{2}(16)\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \frac{16\pi}{3} - 4\sqrt{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds intersection points and subtended angle $\frac{2\pi}{3}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Semicircular region formed by disk and perpendicular bisector.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving x >= 4 from modulus inequality.

walkthrough.text:
Expand squared distances:
$$x^2 + y^2 \geqslant (8 - x)^2 + y^2$$
$$x^2 \geqslant 64 - 16x + x^2$$

Simplify:
$$16x \geqslant 64 \implies x \geqslant 4$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Semicircle geometry and exact area.

hints: Line $x = 4$ passes through the centre, dividing the disk into two semicircles.

walkthrough.text:
Identify centre and relationship to boundary line:
$$\text{Centre } = (4, 2), \quad \text{Radius } R = 3$$
$$\text{The line } x = 4 \text{ passes through the centre, creating a semicircle for } x \geqslant 4.$$

Calculate exact area:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \pi R^2 = \frac{1}{2} \pi (9) = \frac{9\pi}{2}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Observes $x = 4$ passes through centre forming a semicircle.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Finding defining inequalities and boundary intersection points.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Writing defining inequalities for combined region.

walkthrough.text:
Write the disk inequality:
$$|z - (-2 + \mathrm{i})| \leqslant 3 \implies |z + 2 - \mathrm{i}| \leqslant 3$$

Write the horizontal half-plane inequality:
$$\operatorname{Im}(z) \leqslant -1$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding intersection points of boundary circle and horizontal line.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $y = -1$ into circle equation:
$$(x + 2)^2 + (-1 - 1)^2 = 9 \implies (x + 2)^2 + 4 = 9$$
$$(x + 2)^2 = 5$$

Solve for $x$:
$$x + 2 = \pm\sqrt{5} \implies x = -2 \pm \sqrt{5}$$
$$\text{Intersection points: } (-2 + \sqrt{5}, -1) \text{ and } (-2 - \sqrt{5}, -1)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Circle disk and shifted ray angle boundaries.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving initial point of ray lies strictly inside circle.

hints: Centre is $3\mathrm{i}$ and initial point is $1 + 2\mathrm{i}$.
Since $\sqrt{2} < 2$, the initial point is strictly inside the circle.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate distance from centre to initial point:
$$|(1 + 2\mathrm{i}) - 3\mathrm{i}| = |1 - \mathrm{i}| = \sqrt{1^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{2}$$

Compare with radius:
$$\text{Since } \sqrt{2} < 2, \text{ the point } 1 + 2\mathrm{i} \text{ lies strictly inside the circle.}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding highest point on circle and checking argument constraint.

hints: Argument is $\pi - \arctan(3) \approx 1.8925 \text{ rad}$, which lies between $\frac{\pi}{4} \approx 0.785$ and $\frac{3\pi}{4} \approx 2.356$.

walkthrough.text:
Locate highest point on the circle:
$$\text{Centre } (0, 3), \text{Radius } 2 \implies \text{Highest point is } (0, 5) \text{ or } 5\mathrm{i}$$

Evaluate argument from $1 + 2\mathrm{i}$:
$$z - z_0 = 5\mathrm{i} - (1 + 2\mathrm{i}) = -1 + 3\mathrm{i}$$
$$\arg(-1 + 3\mathrm{i}) = \pi - \arctan(3) \approx 1.89 \text{ rad}$$
$$\text{Since } \frac{\pi}{4} \approx 0.79 \leqslant 1.89 \leqslant \frac{3\pi}{4} \approx 2.36, \text{ the point satisfies the inequality.}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Circle disk and perpendicular bisector distance analysis.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Deriving linear half-plane from perpendicular bisector.

walkthrough.text:
Expand squared distances:
$$(x - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 \leqslant (x + 3)^2 + (y - 4)^2$$
$$x^2 - 6x + 9 + y^2 + 4y + 4 \leqslant x^2 + 6x + 9 + y^2 - 8y + 16$$

Simplify:
$$-6x + 4y + 13 \leqslant 6x - 8y + 25 \implies 12y \leqslant 12x + 12 \implies y \leqslant x + 1$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Perpendicular distance from centre to boundary line.

hints: Line is $x - y + 1 = 0$ and point is centre $(3, -2)$.
Since $3\sqrt{2} \approx 4.24 > 2$ (radius), the line does not intersect the circle.

walkthrough.text:
Apply perpendicular distance formula from $(3, -2)$ to $x - y + 1 = 0$:
$$d = \frac{|3 - (-2) + 1|}{\sqrt{1^2 + (-1)^2}} = \frac{6}{\sqrt{2}} = 3\sqrt{2}$$

Compare distance with radius $R = 2$:
$$\text{Since } d = 3\sqrt{2} > 2, \text{ the line does not intersect the circle (the entire disk lies in the region).}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes line does not intersect circle.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Sector area/perimeter and exact surd chord length.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Sector area and perimeter calculations.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate area of sector:
$$\Delta\theta = \frac{\pi}{3} - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{6}$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(4^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{4\pi}{3}$$

Calculate perimeter:
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2(4) + 4\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = 8 + \frac{2\pi}{3}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Arc endpoint coordinates and exact chord length.

walkthrough.text:
Determine exact coordinates of endpoints:
$$z_A = 4\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{6} + \mathrm{i}\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = 2\sqrt{3} + 2\mathrm{i} \implies A(2\sqrt{3}, 2)$$
$$z_B = 4\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{3} + \mathrm{i}\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 2 + 2\sqrt{3}\mathrm{i} \implies B(2, 2\sqrt{3})$$

Calculate chord length using cosine rule:
$$AB^2 = 4^2 + 4^2 - 2(4)(4)\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = 32 - 16\sqrt{3}$$
$$AB = \sqrt{32 - 16\sqrt{3}} = 2\sqrt{6} - 2\sqrt{2}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Intersection points and exact overlapping lens area between two disks.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding intersection points of two overlapping circles.

walkthrough.text:
Subtract circle equations to find common chord line:
$$(x^2 + y^2) - ((x - 2)^2 + y^2) = 4 - 4$$
$$4x - 4 = 0 \implies x = 1$$

Solve for $y$:
$$1^2 + y^2 = 4 \implies y^2 = 3 \implies y = \pm\sqrt{3}$$
$$\text{Intersection points: } (1, \sqrt{3}) \text{ and } (1, -\sqrt{3})$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Calculating exact area of overlapping lens.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate central angle for one circle:
$$\cos\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \implies \frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{\pi}{3} \implies \theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}$$

Calculate area of two identical segments:
$$\text{Segment Area} = \frac{1}{2}(2^2)\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \frac{4\pi}{3} - \sqrt{3}$$
$$\text{Total Area} = 2\left(\frac{4\pi}{3} - \sqrt{3}\right) = \frac{8\pi}{3} - 2\sqrt{3}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Region bounded by circle, ray, and line with vertices and exact sector area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving ray passes through circle centre.

hints: Substitute $(2, 2)$ into $y = x$ to verify containment.

walkthrough.text:
Identify centre of circle:
$$|z - (2 + 2\mathrm{i})| \leqslant 2 \implies \text{Centre } C(2, 2), \quad \text{Radius } R = 2$$

Verify ray passes through centre:
$$\arg(z) = \frac{\pi}{4} \implies y = x \quad (x > 0)$$
$$\text{At } C(2, 2), y = 2 = x \text{ and } x > 0, \text{ so ray passes through centre.}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding Cartesian coordinates of region boundary vertices.

hints: Vertex 2 is top of circle on $x = 2$: $(2, 2 + 2) = (2, 4)$.
Vertex 3 is circle intersection with $y = x$ for $x \leqslant 2$: $(x - 2)^2 + (x - 2)^2 = 4 \implies x = 2 - \sqrt{2}$, giving $(2 - \sqrt{2}, 2 - \sqrt{2})$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify vertices on $x = 2$:
$$V_1 = (2, 2) \quad \text{and} \quad V_2 = (2, 4)$$

Find intersection of circle and $y = x$ for $x \leqslant 2$:
$$2(x - 2)^2 = 4 \implies (x - 2)^2 = 2 \implies x = 2 - \sqrt{2}$$
$$V_3 = (2 - \sqrt{2}, 2 - \sqrt{2})$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding central angle and exact sector area.

hints: Angle of vertical line $x = 2$ going up is $\frac{\pi}{2}$.
Angle of ray $y = x$ going southwest from centre is $\frac{5\pi}{4}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate central angle between boundary radii:
$$\Delta\theta = \frac{5\pi}{4} - \frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{3\pi}{4}$$

Calculate exact sector area:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} R^2 \Delta\theta = \frac{1}{2}(4)\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{3\pi}{2}$$
